---
title: "Figure 6: Cohort-scale compartment localisation"
output: R markdown file
---

## Purpose

Subject-level TAGM visualisation, weighted multinomial localisation with held-out subjects, compartment summaries, Jensen–Shannon divergence, external abundance comparisons and common-space PCA. GO:CC ranked enrichment supporting Supplementary Figure S5 is also included.

## Access and execution

This code is for inspection. Restricted participant-level inputs and intermediate objects are not included. 

## Inputs and dependencies

- `localisation_Apr26.csv`: produced by `scriptforscreen.R`.
- `MAI_prot_model_new.rds`: SummarizedExperiment obtain, available at proteomeXchange
- `demogs`: restricted subject metadata (`Subject`, `Group`, `age_death`, `msex`, `pmi`).
- `Johnson22_prots_full.xlsx`: Johnson et al., 2022. external bulk-proteomics file, downloaded from [LINK] the available supplementary data section.

- GO:CC gene sets from msigdbr are retrieved at execution, using the original annotation/software versions.

```{r display-settings, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

## Load local model inputs and marker labels

Explicit handoff replaces session-only inputs. Marker labels come from the assignments actually used in the TAGM script, not a recreated curation procedure.

## Prepare protein intensities and proportional profiles

```{r protein-profiles}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)

### load my MAI prot RDS as se_log_07
se_log2_07 <- readRDS("MAI_prot_model_new.rds")
se_log2_07 #Summarised experiment, global filter of <0.7 missingness, unimputed and MAI_imputed stored here (both log scaled)

# 2) Extract the imputed assay data and back-transform
MAI_raw <- 2^(assay(se_log2_07, "MAI_imputed")) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% #convert to dataframe
  rownames_to_column("feature_id") %>% #set the proteins as a column
  pivot_longer(-feature_id, names_to = "SampleID", values_to = "value") #pivot long to join with metadata

# 3) extract row/col metadata from SE
rd <- rowData(se_log2_07) %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("feature_id")
cd <- colData(se_log2_07) %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("SampleID")

# 4) Join metadata to assay
long <- MAI_raw %>% #joing long assays with row data
  left_join(rd, by = "feature_id") %>%
  left_join(cd, by = "SampleID") %>%
  left_join(demogs %>% dplyr::select(Subject, Group), by = "Subject")

#sum normalise 
prop <- long %>%
  mutate(log2Quant = log2(value)) %>%
  group_by(Subject, feature_id) %>%
  mutate(sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
         prop = value / sum) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Figure 6A: Before/after TAGM t-SNE

Subject H8 is the manuscript example; seed 6, perplexity 50, theta 0.5 and fraction-column scaling are retained.

```{r tagm-tsne}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(Rtsne)

## ---------------------------
## 1) Filter subject H8 (source exemplar)
## ---------------------------
df_H8 <- tagm_df %>% filter(Subject == "H8")

## ---------------------------
## 2) Build proportional matrix
## ---------------------------
prop_mat <- df_H8 %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein.Group, Fraction, prop) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Fraction) %>%
  summarise(prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Fraction, values_from = prop) %>%
  mutate(across(-Protein.Group, as.numeric)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Protein.Group")

## clean matrix
prop_mat <- prop_mat[complete.cases(prop_mat), ]

## ---------------------------
## 3) t-SNE
## ---------------------------
mat_scaled <- scale(prop_mat)

set.seed(6)

tsne_out <- Rtsne(mat_scaled, dims = 2, perplexity = 50, theta = 0.5, pca = TRUE, check_duplicates = FALSE)

df_tsne <- as.data.frame(tsne_out$Y) %>%
  setNames(c("tSNE1", "tSNE2")) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Protein.Group")

df_tsne$Protein.Group <- rownames(mat_scaled)

## ---------------------------
## 4) Labels
## ---------------------------
labels_df <- df_H8 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Protein.Group,
    markers,
    tagm.map.allocation.pred,
    overall_prob) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    label_before = ifelse(is.na(markers), "unknown", markers),
    label_after = case_when(
      overall_prob >= 0.95 ~ tagm.map.allocation.pred,
      TRUE ~ "unknown"))

## ---------------------------
## 5) Merge t-SNE + labels
## ---------------------------
df_plot <- df_tsne %>%
  left_join(labels_df, by = "Protein.Group")

## ---------------------------
## 6) Long format with ordered panels
## ---------------------------
df_plot_long <- bind_rows(
  df_plot %>%
    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      tSNE1,
      tSNE2,
      label = label_before,
      panel = "Before (markers)"),
  
  df_plot %>%
    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      tSNE1,
      tSNE2,
      label = label_after,
      panel = "After (TAGM ≥ 0.95)")) %>%
  mutate(
    panel = factor(
      panel,
      levels = c("Before (markers)", "After (TAGM ≥ 0.95)")))

## ---------------------------
## 7) Palette
## ---------------------------
plot_palette <- c(marker_palette, "unknown" = "grey85")

## ---------------------------
## 8) Plot
## ---------------------------
H8 <- ggplot(df_plot_long, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2)) +
  
  geom_point(
    data = df_plot_long %>% filter(label == "unknown"),
    aes(colour = label),
    alpha = 0.1,
    size = 1.5) +
  
  geom_point(
    data = df_plot_long %>% filter(label != "unknown"),
    aes(colour = label),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 2.5) +
  
  scale_colour_manual(values = plot_palette, drop = FALSE) +
  
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "fixed") +
  
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  
  labs(
    title = "",
    subtitle = "",
    x = "t-SNE 1",
    y = "t-SNE 2",
    colour = "Compartment") +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",

    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),

    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    strip.background = element_blank(),

    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),

    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10))
```


## Figure 6B: Subject-level cross-validation

The model predicts TAGM allocations with allocated-class probability weights. Test folds contain up to five subjects at a time, and training uses up to 20 of the remaining subjects (19 for some control folds after G2 exclusion). Accuracy measures agreement with original TAGM-MAP output labels.

```{r oos-model}
# ============================================================
# Model explanation
# ============================================================
# 1) A weighted multinomial GLM:
#       compartment_class (k=11) ~ prop in fraction + covariates
# where each row is weighted by TAGM confidence for that row (Subject-protein).
#
# 2) Subject-level CV with TRAIN=20 subjects, TEST=5 subjects (within each disease group), generating 
# OUT-OF-SAMPLE predictions for everyone. 
# This should capture inter-individual prediction stability and uncertainty in localisation prediction
# ============================================================

# -------------------- Packages ------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast grouping + joins for big data
library(nnet)         # multinomial GLM via multinom()
library(ggplot2)      # plotting
library(ggridges)     # ridge plots

# A) -------------------- Data prep -----------------------------
#get sum normalised quant
tagm_df_prop <- tagm_df %>% filter(!is.na(Group)) %>%
  #remove curated marker assignments from training, where weight=1
  filter(markers == "unknown") %>% 
  relocate(prop, .after = Genes)

dt <- data.table::as.data.table(tagm_df_prop)  # convert to data.table for speed / memory efficiency

# Define outcome label y (the TAGM-MAP allocation is one of 11 class labels)
dt[, y := factor(tagm.map.allocation)] 

# Define variables  
dt[, cond := factor(Group)]     # disease condition (adjust if your column is named differently)
dt[, sex := factor(msex)]     # sex as factor (0/1 -> categorical)
dt[, age := age_death]      # numeric
dt[, post_m := pmi]       # numeric (rename to avoid confusion with the data.table 'pmi' symbol)
dt[, frac := as.character(Fraction)] #fraction label
dt[, prop := prop]     #numeric proportion of protein in fraction

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# B) Build weights: w = posterior probability of the allocated class from tagm prediction
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Weighting reduces the impact of uncertain TAGM assignments on model training

# extract compartment probability columns for weighting
prob_cols <- intersect(names(dt), levels(dt$y))  

# for each row, find the probability column corresponding to its assigned class, y
idx <- match(as.character(dt$y), prob_cols) #idx is the column index in prob_cols for that row’s class.

# pull out the per-row weight (posterior probability of the allocated class). cbind() builds the row/col coordinate to extract from the probability matrix.
dt[, w := as.numeric(as.matrix(dt[, ..prob_cols])[cbind(.I, idx)])]

# sanity checks:
summary(dt$w)     # check distribution
table(is.na(dt$w))  # ensure weights were successfully created

#---------- pivot wide for proportional profiles per subject gene  ----------
# so the model can use the complete fractionation profile to predict the compartment

# Keep only what we need for profile + labels/covars
base_cols <- c("Subject","Genes","cond","sex","age","post_m","y","w","frac","prop")
dt0 <- dt[, ..base_cols]
#Wide: one row per Subject x Gene with columns prop_1p...prop_7p
dt_wide <- dcast(dt0, Subject + Genes + cond + sex + age + post_m + y + w 
                 ~ frac, value.var = "prop", fill = 0)

# name proportion in frac columns to prop_<fraction>
frac_levels <- setdiff(names(dt_wide), c("Subject","Genes","cond","sex","age","post_m","y","w"))
setnames(dt_wide, frac_levels, paste0("prop_", frac_levels))

# ============================================================
# C) Cross-validation: TRAIN 20 subjects, TEST 5 subjects, within each cond
# ============================================================
# We want OUT-OF-SAMPLE predictions:
# each subject should appear in the TEST set at least once to get a held-out prediction.
#
# This is performed within disease group (cond)
#
# - For each disease group:
#   - Partition subjects into splits of ~5 (these will be the TEST sets).
#   - For each split:
#       - TRAIN = sample 20 subjects from the remaining subjects in that disease group
#         (if fewer than 20 are available, train on all remaining).
#       - Fit model on TRAIN rows.
#       - Predict probabilities on TEST rows (OUT-OF-SAMPLE).
# - Store predictions and later filter to proteins of interest.
# ============================================================

set.seed(1)  #reproducible subject splits

# Choose which groups to run (adjust levels if needed)
groups_to_run <- levels(dt$cond) #"AD-DEM" "CON"  "RES"  

# list to store out-of-sample probability predictions for all groups/folds
oos_pred_list <- list()

# list to store fold-level performance metrics (optional)
perform_list <- list()

# loop over disease groups (CON / AD-DEM / RES)
for (g in groups_to_run) {

  ### PERFORM SPLIT
  dt_g <- dt_wide[cond == g] # subset to this disease group only
  subj_g <- unique(dt_g$Subject) # extract subject list within this group
  if (length(subj_g) < 6) next  #cannot hold out 5 if fewer than 6 subjects exist
  subj_g <- sample(subj_g) # shuffle subjects so test chunks are random
  test_chunks <- split(subj_g, ceiling(seq_along(subj_g) / 5)) # split into chunks of 5 test subjects

  # Loop over each test chunk (each is one out-of-sample evaluation)
  for (fold_i in seq_along(test_chunks)) {

    test_subj <- test_chunks[[fold_i]]             #TEST = 5 subjects 
    remaining <- setdiff(subj_g, test_subj)      # subjects available for training

    # TRAIN = sample 20 subjects from remaining if possible, else use all remaining
    train_subj <- if (length(remaining) >= 20) sample(remaining, 20) else remaining

    # Create training and test row sets (row-level data, split by Subject)
    train_dt <- dt_g[Subject %in% train_subj]
    test_dt  <- dt_g[Subject %in% test_subj]

    ### Build weighted multinomial GLM on training rows
    #This learns how compartment depends on fractionation profile and covars, weighted by TAGM posteror
    # compartment ~ proportion in fractions 1-7, sex, age, and post-mortem interval

    prop_feature_cols <- grep("^prop_", names(dt_g), value = TRUE) #fractionation profile
    
    formula <- as.formula(paste(
      "y ~", paste(c(prop_feature_cols, "sex", "age", "post_m"), collapse = " + ")))
    
    ### FIT MODEL 
    fit <- multinom(formula, data = train_dt, weights = w, maxit = 200, trace = FALSE)

    ### Evaluate out-of-sample classification on the test set (accuracy)
    pred_class <- predict(fit, newdata = test_dt, type = "class")
    # accuracy is weighted by TAGM confidence (matching a higher confidence assigment contributes more)
    acc_w <- with(test_dt, weighted.mean(pred_class == y, w, na.rm = TRUE))

    perform_list[[length(perform_list) + 1]] <- data.table(
      cond = g,
      fold = fold_i,
      n_train_subjects = length(train_subj),
      n_test_subjects  = length(test_subj),
      n_train_rows = nrow(train_dt),
      n_test_rows  = nrow(test_dt),
      acc_w = acc_w)

    # Get out-of-sample predicted probabilities for each test row
    # This is what is used to build probability distributions per protein.
    pr <- predict(fit, newdata = test_dt, type = "probs")   #matrix: n_test_rows × k_classes

    pr_dt <- as.data.table(pr)                              # convert probs to data.table

    # Attach identifiers so this can be aggregated later
    pr_dt[, `:=`(
      cond    = g,                     # disease group
      fold    = fold_i,                # which test chunk
      Subject = test_dt$Subject,        # subject id for each row
      Genes   = test_dt$Genes,          # gene for each row
      row_w   = test_dt$w               # TAGM confidence weight for the row (optional for aggregation)
    )]

    # Store out-of-sample predictions
    oos_pred_list[[length(oos_pred_list) + 1]] <- pr_dt
  }
}

### STORE all out-of-sample predictions into one table
oos_pred <- rbindlist(oos_pred_list, fill = TRUE)
unique(oos_pred$Genes)


# Combine performance metrics (to assess accuracy)
performance <- rbindlist(perform_list, fill = TRUE)
range(performance$acc_w)

# Inspect
performance[, .(mean_acc_w = mean(acc_w, na.rm = TRUE)), by = cond]
performance[, .(mean_acc = mean(acc_w), sd_acc = sd(acc_w)), by = cond]

```

## Figure 6B: Plot held-out accuracy

Only the observed fold-accuracy points are implemented in the supplied source. The lower reference/permutation points and schematic visible in the manuscript need their separate source.

```{r oos-accuracy}

means <- performance %>%
  group_by(cond) %>%
  summarise(mean_acc = mean(acc_w),
    SD = sd(acc_w), .groups = "drop")
means$x <- c(1, 2, 3)

accuracy <- ggplot(
  performance,
  aes(x = factor(cond, levels = c("CON", "RES", "AD-DEM")),
    y = acc_w, fill = cond, colour = cond)) +

  ## individual folds
  geom_point(
    shape = 21,
    colour = "black",
    aes(fill = cond),
    size = 3,
    stroke = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.7,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.03, height = 0)) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = condition_palette) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = condition_palette) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +

  labs(x = NULL, y = "Weighted accuracy") +

  theme_classic( base_family = "Helvetica", base_size = 10) +

  theme(legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10 ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",size = 10),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10))
```

## Figure 6C: Compartment counts (n confident) and median probabilities

```{r compartment-summaries}
library(ggrepel)

## ----------------------------------------
## Mean OOS probability per Gene
## ----------------------------------------
plot_df <- oos_long %>%
  group_by(compartment, Genes) %>%
  summarise(median_oos_prob = median(oos_prob, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = names(marker_palette)))

# darker marker palette
library(colorspace)
marker_palette_dark <- darken(marker_palette, amount = 0.35)

## ----------------------------------------
## Label Top 5 genes per compartment
## ----------------------------------------
label_df <- plot_df %>%
  group_by(compartment) %>%
  slice_max(median_oos_prob,
            n = 5,
            with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()

## ----------------------------------------
## Violin plot
## ----------------------------------------
violin <- ggplot(plot_df,
                 aes(x = compartment, y = median_oos_prob,
                     fill = compartment, colour = compartment)) +

  geom_violin(
    alpha = 0.35,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    trim = TRUE,
    scale = "width") +

    width = 0.12,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.8,

  data = label_df,

  shape = 21,
  colour = "black",
  stroke = 0.3,
  size = 2.5,
  alpha = 0.8) +

  geom_text_repel(
  data = label_df,
  aes(label = Genes, colour = compartment),
  size = 3,

    legend.position = "none",

    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),

    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

violin
```

## Figure 6D: SNRPA and SCAI probability distributions


```{r snrpa-scai-probabilities}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggridges)
library(patchwork)

# -----------------------------
# 1) Prepare data
# -----------------------------
SNRPA_filt <- oos_long %>% 
  filter(Genes == "SNRPA",
    compartment %in% c("Nucleus", "Ribosome", "Cytosol")) %>%
  mutate(cond = factor(cond, levels = c("AD-DEM", "RES", "CON")))

SCAI_filt <- oos_long %>% 
  filter(Genes == "SCAI",
    compartment %in% c("Presynapse", "Postsynapse","Cytosol")) %>%
  mutate(cond = factor(cond, levels = c("AD-DEM", "RES", "CON")))


#shared x-axis limits
```

## Supplementary Figure S5: GO:CC ranked enrichment

mean-probability rankings, pathway sizes 100–300, positive enrichment and nPermSimple=10000. Seed =3

```{r oos-ranked-enrichment}

#create ranked table (rank proteins within compartment by mean oos prob)
rank_table <- oos_long %>%
  group_by(compartment, Genes) %>%
  summarise(n_subjects = n(),
    mean_prob = mean(oos_prob, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(rowmeta, by = "Genes")

#build ranked vectors
ranks_by_compartment <- rank_table %>%
  group_by(compartment) %>%
  summarise(ranks = list(sort(setNames(mean_prob, Genes), decreasing = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop")

## extract GO pathways
go_cc_pathways <- msigdbr(
  species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C5", subcategory = "GO:CC") %>%
  dplyr::select(gs_name, gene_symbol) %>% distinct() %>%
  group_by(gs_name) %>%
  summarise(genes = list(unique(gene_symbol)), .groups="drop") %>%
  tibble::deframe()

# restrict to genes in each ranking
filter_pathways_to_universe <- function(pathways, universe){
  pathways2 <- lapply(pathways, intersect, y = universe)
  pathways2[lengths(pathways2) >= 100]

}

# Run FGSEA
set.seed(3)
ranks_by_compartment <- ranks_by_compartment %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pathways = list(
      filter_pathways_to_universe(
        go_cc_pathways, names(ranks))),
    fgsea = list(
      fgsea(pathways = pathways,
        stats = ranks,
        scoreType = "pos",
        minSize = 100,
        maxSize = 300,
        nPermSimple = 10000))) %>% ungroup()

fgsea_tidy <- ranks_by_compartment %>%
  dplyr::select(compartment, fgsea) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(fgsea) %>%
  filter(NES > 0, padj < 0.05, !is.na(log2err)) %>% arrange(desc(NES)) 

fgsea_tidy %>% group_by(compartment) %>% arrange(desc(size))

fgsea_top2 <- fgsea_tidy %>%
  group_by(pathway) %>%
  slice_max(NES, n = 2, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>% arrange(compartment, desc(size))
```

## Figure 6E: Jensen–Shannon divergence

```{r js-divergence}
###----------- DIVERGENCE -----------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(tidytext)

###----------------------------
### Mean localisation profile
###----------------------------

mean_prob <- oos_long %>%
  group_by(cond, Genes, compartment) %>%
  summarise(mean_prob = mean(oos_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = compartment,
    values_from = mean_prob,
    values_fill = 0)

feat_cols <- setdiff(names(mean_prob), c("Genes","cond"))

###------------------------------
### Jensen-Shannon divergence calculation
###-----------------------------

jsd_vec <- function(p, q, eps = 1e-12){ #add a small epsilon value to ensure non-zero

  p <- (p + eps) / sum(p)
  q <- (q + eps) / sum(q)

  m <- (p + q)/2

  0.5 * sum(p * log(p / m)) +
  0.5 * sum(q * log(q / m))
}

###------------------------------
### Function for one comparison
###------------------------------

calc_jsd <- function(df, cond1, cond2){

  p1 <- df %>% filter(cond == cond1)
  p2 <- df %>% filter(cond == cond2)

  merged <- inner_join(p1, p2, by = "Genes", suffix = c("_1","_2"))
  
  cols1 <- paste0(feat_cols, "_1")
  cols2 <- paste0(feat_cols, "_2")

  merged$JSD <- mapply(
    function(i){ 
      jsd_vec( #applies JSD calclation to columns
        as.numeric(merged[i, cols1]),
        as.numeric(merged[i, cols2]))
    },
    seq_len(nrow(merged)))

   merged %>%
    transmute(Genes,
      contrast = paste(cond1, "vs", cond2), JSD)

}

###----------------------------
### Run all three contrasts and view
###----------------------------

js_long <- bind_rows(
  calc_jsd(mean_prob, "AD-DEM", "CON"),
  calc_jsd(mean_prob, "AD-DEM", "RES"),
  calc_jsd(mean_prob, "CON", "RES"))

js_long %>% arrange(desc(JSD))

#This can be found in supplementary
#write_csv(js_long, "JSD.csv")
```

## Read in external bulk-proteomics statistics from Johnson et al., 2022


```{r external-bulk-input}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

raw <- read_excel("Johnson_2022.xlsx", col_names = FALSE)
glimpse(raw)

df <- raw[-c(1, 2), ] #clean df (remove header rows first)
colnames(raw)[510]  #this is the ANOVA P-Value column
colnames(df) <- raw[2, ] #assign temporary names for filtering

# filter significant proteins
df_sig <- df %>%
  mutate(ANOVA_P_Value = as.numeric(ANOVA_P_Value)) %>% filter(ANOVA_P_Value < 0.05)

sample_cols <- which(raw[1, ] %in% c("AD", "AsymAD", "Control"))
cond_vec <- as.character(unlist(raw[1, sample_cols]))
colnames(df_sig)[sample_cols] <- paste(
  cond_vec,
  colnames(df_sig)[sample_cols],
  sep = "_")

df_long <- df_sig %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(sample_cols),
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "value") %>%
  separate(sample_id, into = c("cond", "sample"), sep = "_") %>%
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value)) %>% distinct() %>%
  mutate(Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON = as.numeric(Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON))

# Extract all necessary cols (for AD vs CON contrast)
sig_AD_con <- df_long %>% filter(Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON < 0.05) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Symbol, `Uniprot Accession`, `AD-Control`, Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON) %>% distinct() %>% 
  mutate(`AD-Control` = as.numeric(`AD-Control`))

glimpse(sig_AD_con)
```

## Figure 6Eiii: Disease-group profiles in PCA space


```{r condition-pca}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(QFeatures)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)


## ---- 1) Marker prep ----
selected_set_clean <- tagm_df %>% filter(markers != "unknown") %>%
  dplyr::select(markers, Protein.Group) %>% distinct() 

plot_palette <- c(marker_palette, "unknown" = "grey80")

## ---- 2) Metadata ----
cd2 <- cd %>%
  dplyr::select(RunID, Subject, Fraction) %>%
  left_join(prop %>% dplyr::select(Subject, Group) %>% distinct(), by = "Subject") %>%
  dplyr::rename(cond = Group)

## ---- 3) Mean profiles WITH condition ----
mean_profile_cond <- MAI_raw %>%
  dplyr::rename(RunID = "SampleID", Protein.Group = "feature_id", Quant = "value") %>%
  left_join(cd2, by = "RunID") %>%
  filter(cond %in% c("AD-DEM", "CON")) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Fraction, cond) %>%
  summarise(mean_Quant = mean(Quant, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unite("Protein_cond", Protein.Group, cond) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Fraction, values_from = mean_Quant) %>%
  mutate(across(-Protein_cond, as.numeric)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Protein_cond")

## ---- 4) QFeatures + sum normalisation ----
qf_mean <- readQFeatures(
  mean_profile_cond %>% rownames_to_column("Protein_cond"),
  quantCols = 2:ncol(mean_profile_cond %>% rownames_to_column("Protein_cond")),
  name = "mean_profile")

qf_mean <- normalize(
  qf_mean,
  i = "mean_profile",
  name = "norm_profile",
  method = "sum")

## ---- 5) PCA ----
se <- qf_mean[["norm_profile"]]
mat <- assay(se)
#restore Protein_cond as rownames
rownames(mat) <- rowData(se)$Protein_cond

pca <- prcomp(mat, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
pct <- summary(pca)$importance[2, ] * 100

## ---- 6) Extract PCA coords ----
df_pca <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:3]) %>%
  setNames(c("PC1", "PC2", "PC3")) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Protein_cond") %>%
  separate(Protein_cond, into = c("Protein.Group", "cond"), sep = "_") %>%
  left_join(selected_set_clean, by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(cond = factor(cond, levels = c("CON", "AD-DEM")),
    markers = ifelse(is.na(markers), "unknown", as.character(markers)),
    markers = factor(markers, levels = c(names(marker_palette), "unknown")))

## ---- 7) Add protein/gene names (for external overlay) ----
df_pca <- df_pca %>%
  left_join(summary_stats %>% dplyr::select(Genes, Protein.Group), by = "Protein.Group")

highlight_genes <- c("CTHRC1", "MDK", "SMOC1") 

df_arrows <- df_pca %>%
  filter(Genes %in% highlight_genes) %>%  
  dplyr::select(Protein.Group, Genes, cond, PC1, PC2) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = cond, values_from = c(PC1, PC2)) %>%
  mutate(curvature = ifelse(Genes == "MDK", -0.2, 0.1))

## ---- 8) Plot ----
p_pca <- ggplot(df_pca, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2)) +
  
  #density background
  stat_density_2d(data = df_pca %>% filter(markers == "unknown"),
    geom = "polygon", fill = "grey70",
    colour = NA, alpha = 0.02, bins = 8) +
  
  # background proteins
  geom_point(data = df_pca %>% filter(markers == "unknown"),
    aes(colour = markers), alpha = 0.02, size = 4) +
  
  #marker proteins
  geom_point(data = df_pca %>% filter(markers != "unknown"),
    aes(fill = markers),
    shape = 21, colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.18, alpha = 0.1, size = 4) +
  
  #proteins of interest
  geom_point(data = df_pca %>% filter(Genes %in% highlight_genes),
    shape = 18, colour = "black", alpha = 0.7, size = 3.5) +
  
  #Gene labels
  #geom_text_repel(data = df_pca %>% filter(Genes %in% highlight_genes),
    #aes(markers = Genes), seed = 30, size = 1.5, 
    #fontface = "bold", colour = "black", max.overlaps = Inf) +

  #Non-MDK arrows
  geom_curve(
  data = df_arrows %>% filter(Genes != "MDK") %>% mutate(cond = "CON"),
  aes(x = PC1_CON,
    y = PC2_CON,
    xend = `PC1_AD-DEM`,
    yend = `PC2_AD-DEM`),
  curvature = 0.15,
  arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
  colour = "black",
  linewidth = 0.6,
  alpha = 0.7,
  inherit.aes = FALSE) +

  #MDK arrow (flipped)
  geom_curve(
  data = df_arrows %>% filter(Genes == "MDK") %>% mutate(cond = "CON"),
  aes(x = PC1_CON,
      y = PC2_CON,
    xend = `PC1_AD-DEM`,
    yend = `PC2_AD-DEM`),
  curvature = -0.2,   #stronger flip helps visually
  arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
  colour = "black",
  linewidth = 0.7,
  alpha = 0.9,
  inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  scale_colour_manual(values = plot_palette, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = plot_palette, drop = FALSE) +
  
  facet_wrap(~factor(cond, levels = c("CON", "AD-DEM")), ncol = 2)  +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", round(pct[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(pct[2], 1), "%)")) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
```

## Figure 6F: Common cohort PCA space

```{r cohort-pca}
mean_profile <- MAI_raw %>%
  dplyr::rename(RunID = "SampleID", Protein.Group = "feature_id", Quant = "value") %>%
  left_join(cd2, by = "RunID") %>%
  
  #normalisation
  group_by(Subject, Protein.Group) %>%
  mutate(prop = Quant / sum(Quant, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  #average across ALL cohort (no disease group split)
  group_by(Protein.Group, Fraction) %>%
  summarise(mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = Fraction, values_from = mean_prop) %>%
  mutate(across(-Protein.Group, as.numeric)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Protein.Group")
```

```{r spatial-density-preparation}
library(dplyr)

##----------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Intersect datasets

external_spatial <- sig_AD_con %>%
  filter(`Uniprot Accession` %in% df_pca$Protein.Group) %>%
  mutate(significance = if_else(
      Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON < 0.05, "Significant", "Background"),
    direction = case_when(
      # define external sigificant LogFC instances
      Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON < 0.05 & `AD-Control` > 0 ~ "Increased in AD",
      Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON < 0.05 & `AD-Control` < 0 ~ "Decreased in AD", 
      TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  dplyr::select(`Uniprot Accession`, significance, direction, `AD-Control`, Holm_Adj_P_Value_AD_CON)

##----------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Add external annotations to PCA dataframe
##----------------------------------------------------------

df_pca_plot <- df_pca %>%
  left_join(external_spatial, by = c("Protein.Group" = "Uniprot Accession")) %>%
  mutate(significance = replace_na(significance, "Background"))

##----------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Base PCA plot (common to all panels)
##----------------------------------------------------------

base_pca <- ggplot(df_pca_plot,
                   aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  ## faint full spatial proteome
  geom_point(colour = "grey90", alpha = 0.05, size = 1) +
  ## compartment markers
  geom_point(data = df_pca_plot %>% filter(markers != "unknown"),
    aes(colour = markers), alpha = 0.15, size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = plot_palette, drop = FALSE) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +

  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", round(pct[1],1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(pct[2],1), "%)"))
```


## Figure 6F: Background and abundance-direction contours


```{r spatial-density-panels}
##----------------------------------------------------------
## Panel A
##----------------------------------------------------------

p_background <-
  base_pca +

  stat_density_2d(
    data = df_pca_plot %>% filter(significance == "Background"),
    geom = "contour",
    bins = 6,
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.6,
    linewidth = 0.8) +
 scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10))


## ------- grey PCA --------
grey_pca <- ggplot(df_pca_plot, aes(PC1, PC2)) +

  geom_point(
    colour = "grey90",
    alpha = 0.1,
    size = 4) +

  theme_classic(
    base_family = "Helvetica",
    base_size = 10) +

  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(pct[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(pct[2], 1), "%)")) +

  theme(legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10))


##----------------------------------------------------------
## Panel B
##----------------------------------------------------------

p_direction <-
  grey_pca +

  stat_density_2d(
    data = df_pca_plot %>% filter(direction == "Increased in AD"),
    geom = "contour",
    bins = 6,
    colour = "#B2182B",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    alpha = 0.7) +

  stat_density_2d(
    data = df_pca_plot %>% filter(direction == "Decreased in AD"),
    geom = "contour",
    bins = 6,
    colour = "#2166AC",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    alpha = 0.7) +
  
 scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10))


##----------------------------------------------------------
## Combine
##----------------------------------------------------------

combined_pca <- ggarrange(
  p_background,
  p_direction,
  ncol = 2,
  labels = c("I", "II"),
  font.label = list(size = 10, face = "bold"),
  align = "hv")

combined_pca
```
